candidate_name: Namibia common-infrastructure gas / gas-to-power plan (offshore Orange Basin associated gas)
sponsor_or_proposer: Government of Namibia in talks with offshore operators (TotalEnergies Venus, Shell Graff/PEL 39); no terminal sponsor named
current_state: Concept/early discussion. After unexpectedly high gas content in Orange Basin oil finds (Reuters, Nov 2024), Namibia is in talks to agree a single common-infrastructure plan, possibly an upscaled domestic gas-to-power scheme rather than a Walvis Bay LNG import terminal. No defined terminal, sponsor, capacity, or location for any LNG import/export facility.
missing_threshold_elements: No identified terminal sponsor; no approximate terminal location/site; no concrete step toward an LNG import or export terminal (the activity is upstream gas monetization + power, not an LNG terminal). Existing GEM Walvis Bay researcher notes already flag this as not yet entry-ready.
watch_for: A named LNG import terminal or FSRU sponsor/site (e.g. successor to Excelerate's Walvis GasPort), or an export/FLNG decision tied to the Venus/Graff developments; a defined gas-to-power + regas package at Walvis Bay or Luderitz with a concrete commitment.
notes: Does NOT meet the add-bar; logged as a watch item only. Distinct from the cancelled Walvis Bay LNG Terminal (T100000130622), which stays cancelled. Luderitz is being positioned as the offshore O&G logistics base (supply base targeted operational ~2028), which is not an LNG terminal.
